3.speaker: Player
3.text: “My fellow Sords, we are here today not as adversaries, but as collaborators. Our purpose? To invest in Gasom, and ensure it invests in you.”

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Gus Manger stood to my right, his silhouette barely distinguishable from the monolithic edifice behind us.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Serge stood to my left, his eyes scanning the crowd with the precision of a hawk.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: The Gasom security had drawn their weapons in anticipation, forming a bristling wall around the perimeter.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: My Presidential Guard, in stark contrast, stood tall and unflinching at the entrance, shielding us from the sea of angry workers surrounding us.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: The shouts of the crowd were deafening, the hostility palpable. Stahler and Horten stood at the forefront with fire in their eyes.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: With a deep breath, I prepared to address them.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: Gus extended a megaphone towards me.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: As we stepped out of the towering front gate of the Gasom facility, I immediately became aware of how tense the situation was.

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “To the hard-working employees of Gasom, we stand with you today. Our shared goal is simple: to demand improved living and working conditions for everyone.”

17.speaker: Player
17.text: “Good people of Narbel, we come here today seeking understanding and progress. We aim to bridge the gap between Gasom and its employees.”

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “Today my team and I are here to listen and engage. We are here to ensure Gasom becomes a beacon of growth, fairness, and prosperity for all its workers.”

19.speaker: Player
19.text: “We are not blind to your struggles. We seek to acknowledge them, address them, and above all, improve them.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “This is not a hollow promise, but a step towards a stronger and more balanced Sordland.”

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “Remember, we are united by a common goal: A prosperous Gasom that cares for its workers. It's a fight we all must face together.”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “Let's turn this impasse into an opportunity -- a chance for real, impactful change. We are here to make that happen.”

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: A group of figures emerged from the crowd, adorned in unmistakable scarlet attire. The Red Youth had arrived.
23.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Ewald_DonatedToFoundation"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true) == false)

24.speaker: Player
24.text: “My fellow Sords, our presence today is not a guarantee of instant change, but rather an effort to better understand the complexity of the issues at hand.”

25.speaker: Player
25.text: “Good people of Narbel, we are here not to placate you with false promises, but to honestly assess the reality and work towards practical solutions.”

26.speaker: Player
26.text: “We recognize that words are not enough, and only through concrete action can we begin to address the challenges you face.”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “Today’s visit, let's be clear, does not mean all your problems will disappear overnight. It's an initial step to gauge the scope of the issues.”

28.speaker: Katarina Horten
28.text: “Speeches and more speeches, from President Rayne! But what exactly was decided today? We need more than pretty words; we need substance!”

32.speaker: Denis Stahler
32.text: “She's right, Mr. President. We need details. What's going to change for the workers?”

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: I realized this was no longer a mere protest. It was a symbol of a broader, more potent struggle.

37.speaker: Katarina Horten
37.text: “Empty words, Rayne! You've shown us nothing concrete today. We're fed up with your hollow rhetoric!”

38.speaker: Denis Stahler
38.text: “All talk and no action, isn't it, Mr. President? How long must the workers wait for real change?”

39.speaker: Gus Manger
39.text: “Now hold on a moment. President Rayne is committed to bringing about real change. His actions and decisions demonstrate this clearly, even if it doesn't fit your narrative!”

52.speaker: Katarina Horten
52.text: “Wasn't it your government that bailed out the elites while workers were left to suffer? Where was our bailout, Mr. President?”

53.speaker: Denis Stahler
53.text: "Let's not forget your conspicuous absence at Bernard Circas' funeral. Your silence spoke volumes. Do you endorse the killing of those who stand up for workers' rights?"

56.speaker: Katarina Horten
56.text: "Is that so, Manger? All we've seen are decisions that favor the likes of you and Ewald Alphonso, not the common workers!"

57.speaker: Denis Stahler
57.text: "It's not about narratives, Mr. Manger. It's about ensuring a fair, dignified life for the working class. Something your policies have consistently failed to do."

58.speaker: Gus Manger
58.text: "Now, now, let's not get too heated. We all know change doesn't happen overnight. President Rayne is doing what he can."

59.speaker: Denis Stahler
59.text: "Time is a luxury we don't have, Mr. President. Each passing day is another day our workers suffer under the heel of inequality."

60.speaker: Katarina Horten
60.text: "Oh, we've seen how much he can do, Manger. A lot for you, President Alphonso and Gasom, nothing for the workers!"

61.speaker: Denis Stahler
61.text: "Change might not happen overnight, Mr. Manger, but it should at least happen! What we've seen so far is the same old corporate favoritism."

62.speaker: Narrator
62.text: Quiet murmurs of discontent began to ripple through the crowd. The workers' faces seemed to turn even stonier.

63.speaker: Narrator
63.text: Despite the sharp words exchanged, the crowd remained eerily calm.

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: I could feel the tension growing. The presence of our guards did little to reassure me.

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: It seemed like they were waiting, their collective breath held in anticipation of something more.

66.speaker: Katarina Horten
66.text: “Your boost to the police force? A disaster! Inexperienced personnel are not only useless, they are dangerous. They're making the situation worse!”
66.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_BoostPolice"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_Funeral_Attend"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false)

67.speaker: Denis Stahler
67.text: "You label peaceful protestors as traitors? These are ordinary citizens expressing their discontent, not some foreign enemies."
67.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_BoostPolice"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_Funeral_Attend"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false)

68.speaker: Player
68.text: “The business bailout was a necessary step to protect the livelihoods of millions of Sords. It was not a decision made lightly.”

69.speaker: Player
69.text: “My absence at Bernard Circas's funeral was not an endorsement of his murder. It was a time of mourning, and political statements were uncalled for.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “I have always valued the right to peaceful protest. Any assertion otherwise is a misunderstanding.”

71.speaker: Player
71.text: “The discussions with Gasom are an ongoing process, and I am committed to finding the best possible outcome for the workers of Narbel.”
71.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true) == false)

72.speaker: Denis Stahler
72.text: "And what about the recent campaign finance bill, Mr. President? It's a direct attack on democracy, effectively silencing smaller parties like ours!"
72.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_BoostPolice"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_Funeral_Attend"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn01_CampaignFinance_Signed"] == true)

73.speaker: Katarina Horten
73.text: "Mr. President, we demand that you support the upcoming Worker's Rights Bill. The labor force of Sordland will be watching your next move closely!"
73.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_BoostPolice"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_Funeral_Attend"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn01_CampaignFinance_Signed"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Health"] == false) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Health"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Health"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == false) == false)

86.speaker: Player
86.text: “As a result of our negotiations, Gasom has committed to improving the living conditions for its workers. This includes providing private housing and ensuring access to healthcare and education.”

87.speaker: Player
87.text: “Gasom has recognized the value of its blue-collar workers and agreed to increase their wages. These hardworking individuals are the backbone of their operations and deserve fair compensation.”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “I am pleased to announce that Gasom will play a crucial role in the recovery of Narbel. They have pledged a significant contribution to local charities.”
88.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true)

89.speaker: Player
89.text: “I know it's hard to believe. But today was a victory."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “A wage increase is not a mere possibility, but a fact. This is a landmark moment.”

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “With this contribution, Gasom is stepping up to play an essential part in the recovery and development of Narbel.”

92.speaker: Player
92.text: “This is a vital step towards building a more resilient workforce.”

93.speaker: Player
93.text: “This is a substantial step towards ensuring well-being and prosperity for all workers, not just Gasom's."

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “The worst-off will benefit under these new initiatives.”

95.speaker: Player
95.text: “Our efforts have borne fruit. Gasom will now provide better housing, healthcare, and education for every worker.”

96.speaker: Player
96.text: “Through hard negotiations, we've secured a commitment from Gasom to significantly better the lives of its employees. Upgraded housing, assured healthcare, and opportunities for education are now guaranteed.”

97.speaker: Player
97.text: “After much deliberation, Gasom has agreed to increase the wages of the blue-collar workers on whose labor its success rests.”

98.speaker: Player
98.text: “In acknowledgment of their indispensable workforce, Gasom has decided to raise the wages of its blue-collar workers.”

99.speaker: Player
99.text: “I have exciting news: Gasom has promised a substantial contribution to local charities, a move that will play a central role in the recovery efforts for Narbel."
99.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true)

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “Gasom's dedication to Narbel's recovery has been cemented with their promise of a large contribution to local charities.”
100.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true)

101.speaker: Player
101.text: “I must admit, we haven't been able to make as much progress with Gasom as we had hoped. But I remain committed to finding a solution.”
101.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true) == false)

102.speaker: Player
102.text: “Rest assured, we are in continuous dialogue with Gasom. I remain steadfast in my pursuit of better conditions for Narbel's workers.”
102.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true) == false)

103.speaker: Player
103.text: “I understand your frustration. Be assured, I will push harder in the negotiations. The well-being of Narbel's workers is my priority.”

104.speaker: Player
104.text: “The journey may be challenging, but I remain dedicated. Our workers deserve better, and I won't rest until we achieve that.”

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: A change came over the crowd. The angry shouts were replaced with cries of disbelief, then joy.

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: The air suddenly felt somewhat lighter. Murmurs of conversation started to percolate through the crowd, signs of animosity dwindling.

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: I could hear the crowd growing restless. They once again broke into discontented murmurs, punctuated by the occasional shout.

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: The crowd roared back to life. I could practically feel the raw anger emanating from them. My guards took a step forward.

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “The effort of this government will go down in history.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “We have all achieved a victory today.”

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “This marks the beginning of a new era for the city.”

124.speaker: Player
124.text: “I would like to announce that I've personally donated a portion of my salary to the Alphonso Foundation. It's a small step, but one that I believe can help those struggling with homelessness and income inequality."
124.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Ewald_DonatedToFoundation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false)

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “I have made the decision to donate part of my own income to the Alphonso Foundation. In a position of power, it's important to lead by example, isn't it? Together, we can make a difference.”
125.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Ewald_DonatedToFoundation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false)

126.speaker: Player
126.text: “You'll be pleased to know that I've allocated a portion of my rather substantial salary to the Alphonso Foundation. It's the least I can do, considering my privileged position.”
126.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Ewald_DonatedToFoundation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false)

127.speaker: Denis Stahler
127.text: "At least you're not hiding your lack of progress anymore. Mere determination won't solve the workers' problems. We need results."

128.speaker: Katarina Horten
128.text: "And until we get them, we will continue to fight!"

129.speaker: Narrator
129.text: The undercurrent of unrest swelled, threatening to surge into a full-blown tempest. The previous calm seemed like a distant memory, an illusion shattered by the harsh reality of discontent.

130.speaker: Player
130.text: “What if I told you I decided to give away a fraction of my salary to the Alphonso Foundation? Would that make you happy?"
130.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Ewald_DonatedToFoundation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false)

131.speaker: Reporter
131.text: "Mr. President, it's no secret that there was a significant divide during the party leadership campaign involving you and former President Alphonso."

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: The sight of them transported me back to my days among the Young Sords, when face-offs with those clad in crimson were frequent.

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: The sight of them triggered nostalgia, memories of days filled with protests and camaraderie during our time at university.

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: I saw a few officers with nervous faces, belying their inexperience. They stood at attention, visibly on edge.

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: Out of nowhere, a man lunged towards me from the crowd.

143.speaker: Player
143.text: “Denis, the focus here is not on narratives or images but on real, tangible changes. It's a process, and we are on the right track.”

144.speaker: Player
144.text: “I understand your skepticism, Denis. But I assure you my administration is devoted to bringing about better conditions for our workers.”

145.speaker: Player
145.text: “You're an academic and a lawyer, Mr. Stahler. What do you really know about the struggles of the working class?”

146.speaker: Player
146.text: “You're right, Denis. The days of corporate favoritism must come to an end. If not overnight, then soon.”

147.speaker: Player
147.text: “Change may not come as quickly as you want, Denis. But your claims of corporate favoritism don't reflect the complexity of the situation.”

148.speaker: Denis Stahler
148.text: "Words, words, and more words, President Rayne. What the workers need are actions, not promises."

149.speaker: Denis Stahler
149.text: "Your words are compelling, President Rayne. But can they truly outweigh the years of corporate dominance?"

150.speaker: Denis Stahler
150.text: "I know that they deserve better than a president who puts corporate interests over human well-being."

151.speaker: Player
151.text: “Change is often slow and gradual. Not all solutions are as immediate and straightforward as you make them out to be.”

152.speaker: Denis Stahler
152.text: "Your indifference is appalling, President Rayne! The working class can't afford the luxury of time you're so fond of."

153.speaker: Katarina Horten
153.text: "We have had it with excuses, President Rayne! The workers of Sordland need immediate solutions!"

155.speaker: Katarina Horten
155.text: "Exactly, Denis. The working class of Sordland is still waiting for those actions."

156.speaker: Katarina Horten
156.text: "Your intentions sound noble, President Rayne. But intentions alone don't feed families or pay bills. We need concrete actions."

157.speaker: Katarina Horten
157.text: "Attacking Mr. Stahler's personal background accomplishes nothing, Mr. President. What do you have to say to the workers of this nation?"

158.speaker: Denis Stahler
158.text: "Then what just happened in that building, President Rayne? Did you advocate for Gasom's workers, or will its executives only be getting richer?"

159.speaker: Denis Stahler
159.text: "Finally, Rayne, you acknowledge the problem! But acknowledging is not enough. We need action."

160.speaker: Katarina Horten
160.text: "So, President Rayne agrees with Denis! But will this realization actually result in action?"

161.speaker: Katarina Horten
161.text: "There are mothers in Narbel who cannot afford to feed their children. Where is the complexity in that?"

177.speaker: Katarina Horten
177.text: "It's clear from your lack of commitment to education that you don't fully comprehend the scope of the challenges faced by our workers' families."
177.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_BoostPolice"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_Funeral_Attend"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn01_CampaignFinance_Signed"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == false)

178.speaker: Denis Stahler
178.text: "Your neglect of our nation's healthcare system will harm millions."
178.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_BoostPolice"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_Funeral_Attend"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn01_CampaignFinance_Signed"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == false) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Health"] == false)

195.speaker: Denis Stahler
195.text: "Furthermore, we want reform! Reduce the election threshold and change the constitution to make a more democratic and fairer nation!"

196.speaker: Player
196.text: "The people of Sordland have elected me to lead. I believe it's crucial to trust the government's judgement in these times of crisis."

197.speaker: Player
197.text: "I understand the concerns and frustrations many of you have. Rest assured, we are here, we are listening, and we are committed to addressing these issues."

198.speaker: Player
198.text: "We must recognize that our country can't solve all its problems at once. We are working hard and making progress, but our troubles won't simply vanish."

199.speaker: Player
199.text: "The campaign finance bill ensures fair funding for democratically elected parties. It's not an attack on democracy but a measure to safeguard it."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "While the increased police force may have its challenges, it's crucial for maintaining peace and order in our society. Their training and experience will improve over time."

207.speaker: Player
207.text: "On healthcare and education, I hear your concerns. While these areas may not be our immediate focus, we are yet to finalize the government budget and are giving thoughtful consideration to those areas."

214.speaker: Narrator
214.text: Suddenly, a reporter pushed through the crowd, brandishing a microphone towards me.

215.speaker: Reporter
215.text: "The locals of Narbel have suffered under the impact of Gasom for years."

217.speaker: Reporter
217.text: "What concrete steps is Gasom going to take for the benefit of the local community?"

221.speaker: Narrator
221.text: Katarina and Denis raised their hands in a plea for calm, their words nearly lost amidst the turmoil.

235.speaker: Katarina Horten
235.text: "Private housing, healthcare, and education? That's indeed a shift from the status quo, Mr. President."

236.speaker: Denis Stahler
236.text: "If these promises materialize, it could mean a significant improvement in the lives of our comrades at Gasom. This is a start, albeit late. Let's hope it's not mere lip service."

237.speaker: Katarina Horten
237.text: "While I commend this commitment to improve the lives of our Gasom workers, we can only hope this is not just another political gambit."

238.speaker: Denis Stahler
238.text: "So our blue-collar comrades are finally getting the attention they deserve, are they? I must admit, that's a step forward."

239.speaker: Katarina Horten
239.text: "An increase in wages, finally! It's about time, Mr. President. While I appreciate this apparent commitment, let's not pat ourselves on the back just yet."

240.speaker: Denis Stahler
240.text: "But let's not forget, President Rayne, that this is only correcting a long-standing injustice. We will wait and see if these are empty promises or if you truly intend to uphold the rights of our working class."

241.speaker: Katarina Horten
241.text: "Real success will be measured in the paychecks of the workers, not in words spoken here today."

242.speaker: Denis Stahler
242.text: "Charitable contributions, Mr. President? Is that all Gasom can offer?"

243.speaker: Katarina Horten
243.text: "What we need, Mr. President, is not a one-time act of charity, but a sustained commitment to improving the living conditions and wage disparity."

244.speaker: Denis Stahler
244.text: "While the effort is appreciated, these gestures do little to address the structural inequalities faced by the workers. We need systemic change, not charity."

245.speaker: Katarina Horten
245.text: "Gasom's 'charity' must not be used as a smokescreen to cover their ongoing exploitation."

249.speaker: Katarina Horten
249.text: "That's rich, Mr. President! Donating a fraction of your salary while our people continue to suffer. How generous."

250.speaker: Denis Stahler
250.text: "The Alphonso Foundation? More like the President's personal PR project. Let's not forget the true struggles of the Sordish people."

252.speaker: Narrator
252.text: The police began reorganizing their ranks, adopting defensive postures.

253.speaker: Player
253.text: "The past is the past. Personal disagreements have no place in matters of national importance. Our discussions were focused solely on what was best for Sordland."

254.speaker: Player
254.text: "We did have our disagreements, but I won't allow personal matters to obstruct progress. We're both professional enough to separate politics from the welfare of the nation."

255.speaker: Player
255.text: "The rift between former President Alphonso and myself did present obstacles in the negotiations. His reluctance to find common ground was a hurdle."

256.speaker: Reporter
256.text: "Could you shed some light on the possible deal between the Sordish government and Gasom?"

257.speaker: Reporter
257.text: "Did this 'bad blood' influence your negotiations with Gasom?"

259.speaker: Gus Manger
259.text: “To clarify, we tried our best to mediate and negotiate a best possible outcome.”

261.speaker: Reporter
261.text: "What role does the Kingdom of Rizia play in this arrangement?"

262.speaker: Player
262.text: "With all due respect to the Kingdom, I believe Sordland knows whats best for Sordish companies. That's why our government is investing in Gasom alone."

263.speaker: Player
263.text: "Our nation will shoulder the investment for Gasom. It's a bold step, but one that underscores our commitment to self-reliance and autonomy."

264.speaker: Player
264.text: "The government of Sordland has decided to solely invest in Gasom. We believe this will lead to a direct positive impact on the citizens of Sordland."

265.speaker: Player
265.text: "In a show of international cooperation, Sordland and Rizia will jointly invest in Gasom."

266.speaker: Player
266.text: "We are sharing the costs and stakes with Rizia. This way, we're reducing financial pressure and fostering international relationships."

267.speaker: Player
267.text: "Sordland is renewing its ties with the Kingdom of Rizia. Together, we will provide the funding that Gasom and its workers need."

268.speaker: Player
268.text: "Our government has chosen not to invest at this time. We believe Rizia is capable of handling the investment, giving us the opportunity to focus our resources on other pressing issues."

269.speaker: Player
269.text: "Rizia has invested in Sordland before, and they will do it once again. I have faith in the Kingdom and its vision for Gasom."

270.speaker: Player
270.text: "At this time, we won't be investing in Gasom. This decision isn't made lightly, but we're confident Rizia can handle the situation."

271.speaker: Katarina Horten
271.text: "Encouraging, President Rayne. As long as your government's drive to recoup your investment doesn't take precedent over Gasom's struggling labor force."

272.speaker: Denis Stahler
272.text: "A surprising but potentially promising decision, Mr. President. Let's hope your confidence isn't misplaced."

273.speaker: Katarina Horten
273.text: "We will be watching this co-investment closely. Your government will be responsible for keeping its partner's worst tendencies in check."

274.speaker: Denis Stahler
274.text: "A partnership with Rizia? You are aware of the monarchy's history of stamping out disagreements with brute force."

275.speaker: Katarina Horten
275.text: "Relinquishing control to a monarchy!? You are aware of Rizia's history of stamping out disagreements with brute force."

276.speaker: Denis Stahler
276.text: "So, you're putting the fate of our workers in the King of Rizia's hands? That's a dangerous game you're playing, Mr. President."

282.speaker: Player
282.text: "You speak of double standards and yet fail to understand the complexities of governance! It's easy to criticize from the sidelines, but real change requires pragmatism, not idealism."

283.speaker: Player
283.text: "You claim to advocate for the workers, yet undermine our efforts to better their condition. Shouldn't you be supporting the initiatives we've fought for, instead of spreading discontent?"

284.speaker: Player
284.text: "The utopia you dream of won't materialize by mere rhetoric or by attacking those striving for change. It requires understanding the political and economic landscape and making informed decisions."

285.speaker: Player
285.text: "Let's all remember that we're here for the same reason -- to better the lives of our citizens. Let's not allow our differences to blind us to our common goals."

286.speaker: Player
286.text: "The path to progress is challenging and fraught with disagreement, but we must not let this divide us."

287.speaker: Player
287.text: "I understand your frustrations and the urge to voice your concerns. However, let's keep our discourse respectful and constructive."

288.speaker: Serge Wolkner
288.text: "I recommend that we expedite your departure. We must prioritize your safety."

289.speaker: Serge Wolkner
289.text: "It might be a good time to make our way to the convoy, before any potential escalation."

293.speaker: Serge Wolkner
293.text: "It may be best to conclude your address and proceed to the vehicle."

294.speaker: Narrator
294.text: Close by, I noticed a terse exchange between a security officer from Gasom and a member of the Presidential Guard.
294.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_AddressProtestors_Tension"] >= 5  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_MediaBias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_MediaBias"] == true) == false)

295.speaker: Narrator
295.text: Serge craned his neck, his face deep in concentration as he listened to their whispers.

296.speaker: Narrator
296.text: Nearby, a quick, hushed conversation was being had between a Gasom security officer and a Presidential Guard. I followed their eyes to the protestors. Some had calmed down; others still seemed agitated.
296.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_AddressProtestors_Tension"] >= 5  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == false) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_AddressProtestors_Tension"] >= 3  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == false)) and (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_MediaBias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_MediaBias"] == true) == false)

297.speaker: Narrator
297.text: Serge craned his neck, his face deep in concentration as he listened to their whispers.

298.speaker: Narrator
298.text: Nearby, a Gasom security officer and a Presidential Guard member were conversing in hushed tones.
298.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_AddressProtestors_Tension"] >= 5  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_AddressProtestors_Tension"] >= 3  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == false)) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_MediaBias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_MediaBias"] == true) == false)

299.speaker: Narrator
299.text: I saw them glance over the crowd, now calmer but still restless.

300.speaker: Gus Manger
300.text: "I'll stay back and handle things here. You should head to safety."

301.speaker: Gus Manger
301.text: "Mr. President, I'll stay on to further address the crowd. The mood is still tense, but I think I can manage. You should get on your way."

302.speaker: Gus Manger
302.text: "I'll remain here, Mr. President. The crowd seems calmer now, and I believe I can answer their queries and maintain the peace. You should go ahead."

303.speaker: Katarina Horten
303.text: "You can't even face your own people, can you, Mr. President? We expected better."

304.speaker: Denis Stahler
304.text: "Leaving so soon, Rayne? I guess you know when you've been defeated."

305.speaker: Katarina Horten
305.text: "We will hold you accountable to your promises. The troubles of the laborers continue and our union is here to solve them."

306.speaker: Denis Stahler
306.text: "I'm impressed you even came out to speak to us, President Rayne. Most wouldn't. However, this conversation isn't over yet."

307.speaker: Katarina Horten
307.text: "Mr. President, thank you for your willingness to address us. Let's continue these important conversations moving forward."

308.speaker: Denis Stahler
308.text: "You've shown courage today. We'll see if your actions match your words. Until next time."

309.speaker: Player
309.text: "Thank you for looking out for me, Serge. Let's get out of here."

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "Are you sure? Won't running away from this only make the protestors angrier?"

311.speaker: Player
311.text: "I agree, Serge. Tensions can rise quickly in such environments. It's better we make our exit now."

312.speaker: Player
312.text: "Are you sure? Won't running away from this only make the protestors angrier?"

313.speaker: Player
313.text: "You're absolutely right, Serge. Let's not stay here any longer than necessary."

314.speaker: Player
314.text: "Are you sure? Won't running away from this only make the protestors angrier?"

315.speaker: Serge Wolkner
315.text: "Mr. President, the situation is growing increasingly volatile."

316.speaker: Serge Wolkner
316.text: "Sir, the crowd is no longer entirely hostile, but there's still an undercurrent of tension."

317.speaker: Serge Wolkner
317.text: "President Rayne, while the crowd appears somewhat subdued, I would advise we exercise caution."

318.speaker: Reporter
318.text: "Can you clarify the current status of your personal relationship with Ewa-"

319.speaker: Reporter
319.text: "One final question, what is your true personal relationship with Ew-"

329.speaker: Narrator
329.text: Serge left my dazed attacker on the ground and turned to the guards with a look of authority I'd never seen before.

330.speaker: Narrator
330.text: His voice carried over the screams of the crowd. The guards tightened their circle around me, hurriedly pushing me towards the safety of the convoy.

331.speaker: Narrator
331.text: Police and security forces rushed into the melee, swinging batons with indiscriminate ferocity. The Red Youth rushed at them head-on.

332.speaker: Katarina Horten
332.text: "Stop the cops! This isn't going to help!"

334.speaker: Narrator
334.text: Their screams receded into the background as we left the chaotic scene behind.

338.speaker: Gus Manger
338.text: "Back off! You're only making things worse!"

339.speaker: Narrator
339.text: The staff and I were swiftly escorted into the convoy. The protestors and police scattered as our vehicles plowed through the crowd.

340.speaker: Serge Wolkner
340.text: "Into the car, Mr. President! We are leaving NOW!"

341.speaker: Narrator
341.text: Before I could react, Serge sprang in front of me. He swiftly tackled the man to the ground and pinned his hands behind his back.

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: The nervous officers I'd seen before now looked completely overwhelmed. They lashed out left and right, hitting protestors, Red Youth members and their own colleagues alike.

346.speaker: Serge Wolkner
346.text: "Mr. President, if you could please proceed to the vehicle."

347.speaker: Player
347.text: "Yes, the dialogue has only started. I assure you both, my commitment to progress and change is unwavering."

348.speaker: Player
348.text: "Indeed, accountability is the cornerstone of democracy. As your president, I understand that responsibility."

349.speaker: Player
349.text: "Most wouldn't come out because most fear facing the truth. As for the conversation, it's always been going on."

350.speaker: Player
350.text: "My job is to listen and act. As for accountability, isn't that what all governments should be held to? You have my word."

351.speaker: Player
351.text: "Denis, Katarina, I look forward to our continuing conversations."

352.speaker: Player
352.text: "This is a marathon, not a sprint."

356.speaker: Player
356.text: "As an old Red Youth member, I can personally say that the work you do is of utmost importance. Thank you."

357.speaker: Narrator
357.text: Almost immediately, the remaining tension in the crowd dissipated. A few workers nearby broke into scattered applause.

358.speaker: Narrator
358.text: A flutter of whispers rippled through the sea of onlookers, their eyes darting back and forth between us in surprise. A few broke into scattered applause.

359.speaker: Narrator
359.text: Their collective gaze bore into me, awaiting my words.

360.speaker: Narrator
360.text: I turned to the crowd one last time. In their eyes, I saw both flashes of anger and glimmers of hope.

361.speaker: Katarina Horten
361.text: "We have shown courage together. Now we will hold you accountable to your promises. The troubles of the laborers are not over, and neither is the work of our union."

362.speaker: Narrator
362.text: As I readied myself to leave, I turned back to Katarina and Denis a last time.

363.speaker: Narrator
363.text: The initially hesitant clapping grew louder, and jubilant cheers and whistles filled the air. I saw the Red Youth members standing at the edge of the crowd with their arms folded, a hint of approval in their eyes.

364.speaker: Player
364.text: "Together, we can ensure a prosperous future for Sordland."

365.speaker: Narrator
365.text: Serge opened the door of the car and I lowered myself into the seat. The door closed behind me with a thud, sealing off the external noise.

366.speaker: Narrator
366.text: The crowd began to disperse, the individuals breaking away to let our convoy through. The guards took their position nonetheless, forming a human barrier around the vehicle.

367.speaker: Narrator
367.text: The engine purred to life, and we began to move.

371.speaker: Serge Wolkner
371.text: "I had no doubt about your capability to handle this, President Rayne. Still, I was worried for your safety."

372.speaker: Serge Wolkner
372.text: "I'm glad we are safely on our way, Mr. President."

373.speaker: Narrator
373.text: As we started moving, some disgruntled protestors rushed towards us. I could hear shouts and jeers as their fists pounded against the glass windows.

374.speaker: Narrator
374.text: The guards sprang into action, pushing back the unruly crowd.

375.speaker: Narrator
375.text: It was a tense few moments before the convoy was able to navigate away from the tumult.

379.speaker: Player
379.text: "Thanks for your concern, Serge. It was tense, but knowing you and the team were there made all the difference."

380.speaker: Player
380.text: "Serge, in this role, danger comes with the territory. But your concern is appreciated."

381.speaker: Player
381.text: "Don't forget, a President has to face these situations head-on."

382.speaker: Player
382.text: "Thank you, Serge. I don't know what I'd do without you."

383.speaker: Player
383.text: "Agreed, Serge. A job well done by you and the team."

384.speaker: Player
384.text: "A little excitement to keep us on our toes, wasn't it?"

385.speaker: Serge Wolkner
385.text: "We're here to serve and protect, Mr. President. It's a duty we don't take lightly."

386.speaker: Serge Wolkner
386.text: "It's not just part of the job, sir. It's a matter of personal commitment."

387.speaker: Serge Wolkner
387.text: "You're right, sir. It's part of the job, after all."

388.speaker: Serge Wolkner
388.text: "I'm merely doing my job, Mr. President. Ensuring your safety is my top priority."

389.speaker: Serge Wolkner
389.text: "We appreciate your acknowledgement, Mr. President. It's our duty and honor."

390.speaker: Serge Wolkner
390.text: "That's one way to look at it, Mr. President. Keeps the job interesting, to say the least."

391.speaker: Narrator
391.text: The echoing voices of the protesters gradually subsided as we retreated from the scene and left Narbel behind.

402.speaker: Narrator
402.text: Eventually, all fell silent as they waited for Denis and Katarina to respond.

403.speaker: Gus Manger
403.text: "Serge is right, Mr. President. The crowd won't get any calmer if you stick around. You've got to get to safety."

453.speaker: Player
453.text: "Before any of you do anything too rash, I want you to take a good look around you."

454.speaker: Player
454.text: "You are surrounded by police and armed guards. Realistically, what do you hope to accomplish here?"

455.speaker: Player
455.text: "You cannot rise up against the President of Sordland without facing consequences."

457.speaker: Player
457.text: "We are all brothers and sisters in the struggle against greed and exploitation. We must not let ourselves become divided."

458.speaker: Denis Stahler
458.text: "You're going to jump directly to threatening us, President Rayne? Whatever happened to the right to peaceful protest?"

459.speaker: Katarina Horten
459.text: “This only proves that we are right to stand here today. We will not budge until you commit to real change."

460.speaker: Denis Stahler
460.text: "Divided? You're the one walking out of Gasom headquarters surrounded by armed guards."

461.speaker: Player
461.text: "How dare you speak that way to your president! You ingrates have no idea how much I have sacrificed for this country."

463.speaker: Player
463.text: “See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I'm on your side. You can stop whining now."

464.speaker: Player
464.text: “See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I'm on your side. You can stop whining now."

465.speaker: Player
465.text: “See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I'm on your side. You can stop whining now."

466.speaker: Player
466.text: “I'm not going to dignify that with a response. Gasom has done so much for this shithole region, and this is how you people repay it?"
466.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_FreeHousingEducationHealthBenefits"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_IncreasedBlueCollarWages"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_PSnW_Gasom_LocalCharityDonation"] == true) == false)

467.speaker: Player
467.text: "Honestly, these workers are lucky to even have jobs. They shouldn't get greedy."

468.speaker: Player
468.text: "I'm warning you all. Back off now, or there *will* be consequences."

469.speaker: Player
469.text: "Why don't you talk to an actual Gasom employee, Madam Reporter? They'll tell you how grateful they are to work for the best company in Sordland."

472.speaker: Katarina Horten
472.text: "Clearly, we are past the time for reasonable discussion. We must fight for what we believe in!"

476.speaker: Player
476.text: "What the hell are you still doing here, lady? Can't you see it's about to get ugly?"

477.speaker: Denis Stahler
477.text: "The sight of the common people speaking truth to power is anything but 'ugly', Rayne."

480.speaker: Katarina Horten
480.text: "I see. The President won't divulge any information about his closed-door dealings."
